rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One chronology places the Sleepers before Moses and says Moses mentioned them in the Torah, explaining why Jews asked about them.
rows.anchor: قيل إنهم كانوا قبل موسى عليه السلام وإن موسى ذكرهم في التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another chronology says they entered the cave before Jesus, Jesus related their story, and they awoke between Jesus and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: إنهم دخلوا الكهف قبل المسيح وأخبر المسيح بخبرهم ثم بعثوا في الوقت

rows.speaker: القفال عن محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal attributes to Muhammad ibn Ishaq the view that the Sleepers entered the cave after Jesus.
rows.anchor: وحكى القفال هذا القول عن محمد بن إسحاق

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some people claim the Sleepers never died and will remain alive until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: إنهم لم يموتوا ولا يموتون إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: محمد بن موسى الخوارزمي
rows.claim: Al-Khwarizmi says al-Wathiq sent him to the Romans to investigate the purported cave of the Sleepers.
rows.anchor: أن الواثق أنفذه ليعرف حال أصحاب الكهف إلى الروم

rows.speaker: محمد بن موسى الخوارزمي
rows.claim: Al-Khwarizmi reports seeing hair on the bodies' chests and judging the display a contrivance, with corpses preserved against decay.
rows.anchor: فدخلت ورأيت الشعور على صدورهم قال وعرفت أنه تمويه واحتيال

rows.speaker: محمد بن موسى الخوارزمي
rows.claim: The preserved bodies may have been treated with drying medicines such as aloe to prevent their decay.
rows.anchor: عالجوا تلك الجثث بالأدوية المجففة لأبدان الموتى لتصونها عن البلى

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says it is unknown whether the reported site is the actual cave or another place, and Roman identification is no proof.
rows.anchor: والذي عندنا لا يعرف أن ذلك الموضع هو موضع أصحاب الكهف أو موضع آخر

rows.speaker: معاوية
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf relates that Muawiya passed the cave during a Roman campaign and wanted to uncover the Sleepers and see them.
rows.anchor: ذكر في الكشاف عن معاوية أنه غزا الروم فمر بالكهف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas told Muawiya that God had forbidden him to inspect the Sleepers, as He had forbidden someone better than him.
rows.anchor: ليس لك ذلك قد منع الله من هو خير منك

rows.speaker: معاوية
rows.claim: In the report, Muawiya insisted on learning their condition and sent men into the cave; a divinely sent wind burned them.
rows.anchor: فلما دخلوا الكهف بعث الله عليهم ريحا فأحرقتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason cannot establish the Sleepers' era or location; this knowledge requires a revealed text, which is unavailable.
rows.anchor: العلم بذلك الزمان وبذلك المكان ليس للعقل فيه مجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection's possibility rests on God's power over all possible things, knowledge of all universals and particulars, and the possibility of what occurs once occurring at other times.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى قادر على كل الممكنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given those principles, sustaining a person safely through three hundred years of sleep is possible just as keeping someone alive during a day's sleep is possible.
rows.anchor: فكذلك بقاؤه مدة ثلثمائة سنة يجب أن يكون ممكنا بمعنى أن إله العالم يحفظه

rows.speaker: الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Philosophers also allow that unusual celestial configurations could produce rare, extraordinary conditions in sublunary matter.
rows.anchor: لا يبعد وقوع أشكال فلكية غريبة توجب في هيولي عالم الكون والفساد حصول أحوال غريبة نادرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The neighboring surahs present three rare marvels: the bodily night journey, the Sleepers' long sleep, and Jesus' birth without a father.
rows.anchor: هذه السور الثلاثة المتعاقبة اشتمل كل واحد منها على حصول حالة عجيبة نادرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stated argument from divine knowledge and power establishes the possibility of all three marvels.
rows.anchor: والمعتمد في بيان إمكان كل هذه العجائب والغرائب المذكورة في هذه السور الثلاثة المتوالية

rows.speaker: أبو علي بن سينا عن أرسطاطاليس
rows.claim: In the Shifa's discussion of time, Avicenna reports Aristotle's account of a group of godly people experiencing a state like the Sleepers.
rows.anchor: أن أرسطاطاليس الحكيم ذكر أنه عرض لقوم من المتألهين حالة شبيهة بحالة أصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: أبو علي بن سينا
rows.claim: Avicenna says historical records indicate that those people lived before the Companions of the Cave.
rows.anchor: ويدل التاريخ على أنهم كانوا قبل أصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage from this verse through the Moses-and-Khidr story forms one discourse responding to Quraysh leaders who demanded that poor believers be expelled before they would believe.
rows.anchor: إن من هذه الآية إلى قصة موسى والخضر كلام واحد في قصة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rejects the leaders' demand and makes the governing instruction steadfast recitation of the revealed Book and adherence to it, disregarding objections and obstinacy.
rows.anchor: أن يواظب على تلاوة الكتاب الذي أوحاه الله إليه وعلى العمل به وأن لا يلتفت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to recite includes both reading the Book and following its guidance in practice.
rows.anchor: يتناول القراءة ويتناول الإتباع فيكون المعنى الزم قراءة الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that none can change God's words may support forbidding analogical qualification of an explicit text, since the command requires acting on its apparent wording.
rows.anchor: يمكن التمسك بها في إثبات أن تخصيص النص بالقياس غير جائز

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Abu Muslim al-Isfahani's position would make the verse preclude abrogation as well.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل فيجب ألا يتطرق النسخ إليه قلنا هذا هو مذهب أبي مسلم الأصفهاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrogation is not textual alteration: a ruling remains valid until its abrogator arrives, which functions as its endpoint.
rows.anchor: النسخ في الحقيقة ليس بتبديل لأن المنسوخ ثابت في وقته إلى وقت طريان الناسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentators agree that multahad means a refuge or place of recourse.
rows.anchor: اتفقوا على أن الملتحد هو الملجأ

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Lexicographers connect multahad to lahd and ilhad, meaning to incline; mulhid is one who inclines away from religion.
rows.anchor: هو من لحد وألحد إذا مال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means that apart from God there is no refuge in explanation and guidance.
rows.anchor: ولن تجد من دونه ملجأ في البيان والرشاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh leaders said they would believe only if the Prophet expelled the poor, kept them away when the leaders came, and assigned the two groups separate meeting times.
rows.anchor: إن أردت أن نؤمن بك فاطرد هؤلاء الفقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God revealed the instruction not to expel those who call upon Him, commanding their company and honor instead of attending to the unbelievers' demands.
rows.anchor: ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This account is a fresh, independent passage rather than a continuation of the preceding discussion.
rows.anchor: وهذه القصة منقطعة عما قبلها وكلام مبتدأ مستقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel in al-Anam forbids expelling the poor; this verse positively commands keeping company and patiently remaining with them.
rows.anchor: نهي الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم عن طردهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabr fundamentally means restraint; the Prophet prohibited an animal held still as a target to be shot.
rows.anchor: أصل الصبر الحبس ومنه نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن المصبورة

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads al-ghudwah with a damma on the ghayn; the other readers read al-ghadah, and both are Arabic forms.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر بالغدوة بضم الغين والباقون بالغداة وكلاهما لغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of morning and evening is continual observance, illustrated by a saying that someone does nothing morning and evening except insult people.
rows.anchor: المراد كونهم مواظبين على هذا العمل في كل الأوقات كقول القائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes morning and evening as the dawn and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: أن المراد صلاة الفجر والعصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation sees morning awakening as a transition from death to life and evening sleep as life returning to death; the wise remember and thank God then.
rows.anchor: الغداة هي الوقت الذي ينتقل الإنسان فيه من النوم إلى اليقظة وهذا الانتقال شبيه بالانتقال من الموت إلى الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about the eyes not passing over them forbids distancing one's gaze; عن conveys separation, as in the idiom for exceeding one's proper bounds.
rows.anchor: يقال عداه إذا جاوزه ومنه قولهم عدا طوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with the dual subject عينيك derives the verb from the causative or intensive forms أعداه and عداه.
rows.anchor: من أعداه وعداه نقلا بالهمزة وتثقيل الحشو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poetic line using عد witnesses the sense of turning away or passing over.
rows.anchor: فعد عما ترى إذ لا ارتجاع له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command forbids looking down on poor believers or turning one's eyes from them to seek the company and appearance of the wealthy.
rows.anchor: عن أن يزدرى فقراء المؤمنين وأن تنبو عيناه عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wanting worldly adornment is grammatically a circumstantial accusative and means that such conduct would arise only from desire for worldly display.
rows.anchor: { تريد زينة الحيواة الدنيا } نصب في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Asharites cite God saying that He made the person's heart heedless as evidence that God creates ignorance and heedlessness in such hearts.
rows.anchor: احتج أصحابنا بهذه الآية على أنه تعالى هو الذي يخلق الجهل والغفلة في قلوب الجهال

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazila read the wording as God finding the heart heedless, not creating heedlessness in it.
rows.anchor: أنا وجدنا قلبه غافلا وليس المراد خلق الغفلة فيه

rows.speaker: عمرو بن معديكرب الزبيدي
rows.claim: Amr ibn Ma'dikarib illustrates the found-such wording by saying his opponents were not found cowardly, miserly, or unable to answer satire.
rows.anchor: ما وجدناكم جبناء ولا بخلاء ولا مفحمين

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Their first objection is that creating the heedlessness would remove the person's entitlement to blame.
rows.anchor: أنه لو كان كذلك لما استحقوا الذم

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Their second objection cites the following invitation to believe or disbelieve: it would not make sense if God had created the heedlessness.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى قال بعد هذه الآية

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Their third objection says that if God caused heedlessness, following desire should be connected by fa as a consequence, like breaking followed by breaking, rather than by waw.
rows.anchor: لو كان المراد هو أنه تعالى جعل قلبه غافلا

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Their fourth objection is that if God truly made the heart heedless, the act should not be attributed to the person's following his desire.
rows.anchor: ولو كان تعالى أغفل في الحقيقة قلبه لم يجز أن يضاف ذلك إلى اتباعه هواه

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: In answer, the Mu'tazila restate that أغفلنا means that God found the heart heedless rather than producing its heedlessness.
rows.anchor: وليس المارد تحصيل الغفلة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb pattern أفعل is more properly taken as bringing something about than as finding it: causative usage is more frequent and more readily understood.
rows.anchor: مجيء بناء الأفعال بمعنى التكوين أكثر من مجيئه بمعنى الوجدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causative sense is also preferable because knowing a thing depends on its coming to exist; making the form literal for the prior event and figurative for cognition follows that relation.
rows.anchor: جعل اللفظ حقيقة في المتبوع ومجازا في التبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person cannot create a particular heedlessness: to intend heedlessness about a specific thing, one must conceive and thus be conscious of that thing, contradicting heedlessness.
rows.anchor: لا يمكنه القصد إلى إيجاد الغفلة عن كذا إلا مع الشعور بكذا لكن الغفلة عن كذا ضد الشعور بكذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trying to create undirected heedlessness is equally impossible, since it would not explain why one becomes heedless of one object rather than another.
rows.anchor: وإلا لم يكن بأن تحصل له الغفلة عن هذا الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a servant cannot produce heedlessness in himself, God must be the creator of heedlessness, and أغفلنا denotes creation rather than merely finding.
rows.anchor: خالق الغفلات وموجدها في العباد هو الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection from the waw assumes that creating heedlessness necessarily causes desire-following; it does not, since a heedless person may remain hesitant, bewildered, or afraid.
rows.anchor: لا يلزم من حصول الغفلة عن الله حصول متابعة الهوى لاحتمال أن يصير غافلا عن ذكر الله

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal offers a Mu'tazili reading in which God showered worldly goods on them, causing their hearts to become heedless.
rows.anchor: لما صب عليهم الدنيا صبا وأدى ذلك إلى رسوخ الغفلة في قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi replies that if worldly pleasures affect their heedlessness, God caused it by giving them; if they do not affect it, the attribution fails.
rows.anchor: فإن أثر كان أثر إيصال اللذات إليه سببا لحصول الغفلة في قلبه

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal also glosses أغفلنا as leaving the person heedless without marking him with the sign of purity and piety, like an unmarked camel.
rows.anchor: أي تركناه غافلا فلم نسمه بسمة أهل الطهارة والتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says this gloss is equivalent to saying God blackened the heart or whitened the face and therefore does not escape his argument.
rows.anchor: إن قوله أغفلنا قلبه بمنزلة قوله سودنا قلبه وبيضنا وجهه

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: A third al-Qaffal interpretation is that God left the heart with Satan and did not prevent Satan from reaching it.
rows.anchor: أن المراد من قوله أغفلنا قلبه أي خلاه مع الشيطان ولم يمنع الشيطان منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that if this abandonment affects the heedlessness, the divine attribution stands; if it has no effect, it cannot explain the wording.
rows.anchor: إن كان لتلك التخلية أثر في حصول تلك الغفلة فقد صح قولنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worst human state is a heart empty of God's remembrance and filled with desire that turns its attention to created beings.
rows.anchor: شر أحوال الإنسان أن يكون قلبه خاليا عن ذكر الحق ويكون مملوءا من الهوى الداعي إلى الاشتغال بالخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's remembrance is light and remembrance of other things is darkness: God is necessary existence and true light, while contingent beings derive from nonexistence and darkness.
rows.anchor: ذكر الله نور وذكر غيره ظلمة لأن الوجود طبيعة النور والعدم منبع الظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A heart lit by God's remembrance has light; turning to created beings brings darkness, so turning away from God is complete darkness.
rows.anchor: فالقلب إذا أشرق فيه ذكر الله فقد حصل فيه النور والضوء والإشراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this interpretation, أغفلنا describes turning away from God and واتبع هواه describes turning toward created beings.
rows.anchor: الإعراض عن الحق هو المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One gloss of فرطا is exceeding the limit, from فرس فرط, a horse that runs ahead of the others.
rows.anchor: أي مجاوزا للحد من قولهم

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth says فرط describes an affair that is neglected or wasted, as in a poetic line calling an affair فرطا.
rows.anchor: الفرط الأمر الذي يفرط فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poem uses فرطا to mean something wasted or neglected.
rows.anchor: وأمرا خائبا فرطا أي مضيعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that a person neglects the matter needing care, religion, and devotes his activity to worldly life.
rows.anchor: الأمر الذي يلزمه الحفظ له والاهتمام به وهو أمر دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor believers persist in remembrance and turn away from other things, while the wealthy leaders neglect God and follow desire; the Prophet is told to stay with the former and avoid the latter.
rows.anchor: وصف أولئك الفقراء بالمواظبة على ذكر الله والإعراض عن غير ذكر الله

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id says he sat among impoverished Emigrants, some covering one another's nakedness, while one recited Qur'an and the rest listened; the Prophet praised those he was commanded to keep company with.
rows.anchor: كنت جالسا في عصابة من ضعفاء المهاجرين وإن بعضهم ليستر بعضا من العرى

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet gave the poor Emigrants glad tidings of complete light on Judgment Day and entry into Paradise fifty thousand years before the rich.
rows.anchor: أبشروا يا صعاليك المهاجرين بالنور التام يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account of the passage's order says it answers wealthy leaders who conditioned belief on expelling the poor: acceptance benefits them, refusal harms them, and social status is irrelevant.
rows.anchor: إن هذا الدين الحق إنما أتى من عند الله فإن قبلتموه عاد النفع إليكم وإن لم تقبلوه عاد الضرر إليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second account identifies the truth from God as the command to keep company with poor believers and disregard worldly leaders.
rows.anchor: جاءني من عنده أن أصبر نفسي مع هؤلاء الفقراء ولا أطردهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third account connects the passage to the freedom to believe or disbelieve and God's refusal to expel believers to attract unbelieving elites.
rows.anchor: أن الحق الذي جاء من عند الله فمن شاء فليؤمن ومن شاء فليكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that expelling the poor would sacrifice a small harm to them to prevent the greater harm of unbelief is rejected: belief conditional on avoiding the poor is ugly hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: من ترك الإيمان لأجل الحذر من مجالسة الفقراء فإيمانه ليس بإيمان بل هو نفاق قبيح

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazila take the invitation to believe or disbelieve as explicit proof that faith, disbelief, obedience, and sin are left to human choice.
rows.anchor: صريح في أن الأمر في الإيمان والكفر والطاعة والمعصية مفوض إلى العبد واختياره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues that actions require intention and choice, but every intention cannot depend on an earlier one indefinitely; the chain must end in a will God creates necessarily in a person.
rows.anchor: وجب انتهاء تلك القصود وتلك الاختيارت إلى قصد واختيار يخلقه الله تعالى في العبد على سبيل الضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the decisive will exists, the action follows necessarily; when it is absent, the action does not occur, leaving humans compelled in the form of choosers.
rows.anchor: فالإنسان شاء أو لم يشأ إن لم تحصل في قلبه تلك المشيئة الجازمة الخالية عن المعارض لم يترتب الفعل

rows.speaker: أبو حامد الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali presents the objection that people directly experience being able to act if they will and to refrain if they will.
rows.anchor: إني أجد في نفسي وجدانا ضروريا أني إن شئت الفعل قدرت على الفعل وإن شئت الترك قدرت على الترك

rows.speaker: أبو حامد الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali replies that people do not choose whether their will itself arises; it appears without an earlier will, and action follows it necessarily, so both are from God.
rows.anchor: هل تجد من نفسك أنك إن شئت مشيئة الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that an action cannot issue from an agent without intention and motive.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على أن صدور الفعل عن الفاعل بدون القصد والداعي محال

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says the imperative here is a threat and warning, not a grant of choice.
rows.anchor: نقل عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه أنه قال هذه الصيغة تهديد ووعيد وليست بتخيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God neither benefits from believers' faith nor suffers from unbelievers' disbelief; benefit and harm return to people themselves.
rows.anchor: لا ينتفع بإيمان المؤمنين ولا يستضر بكفر الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage moves from describing truth, falsehood, faith, and disbelief to threats for disbelief and false deeds and promises for faith and good deeds.
rows.anchor: أتبعه بذكر الوعيد على الكفر والأعمال الباطلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are those who misplace worship and pride, rejecting truth because poor people accepted it; God has prepared Hell for them.
rows.anchor: وضع العبادة في غير موضعها والأنفة في غير محلها فعندما استحسن بهواه وأنف عن قبول الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A suradīq is a barrier around a tent; the image means the fire encloses them on every side with no escape or opening.
rows.anchor: والسرادق هو الحجزة التي تكون حول الفسطاط فأثبت للنار شيئا شبيها بذلك يحيط بهم من جميع الجهات

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret the enclosing barrier as smoke like the three-branched shade, surrounding the unbelievers before they enter the fire.
rows.anchor: المراد من هذا السرادق الدخان

rows.speaker: حديث مرفوع
rows.claim: A prophetic report glosses the water like molten metal as the dregs of oil.
rows.anchor: قيل في حديث مرفوع إنه دردي الزيت

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud heated a residue taken from the treasury until it glowed and identified it as molten metal.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أنه دخل بيت المال وأخرج نفاثة كانت فيه وأوقد عليها النار حتى تلألأت

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأخفش
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Akhfash define molten metal as anything melted from gold, copper, or silver.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة والأخفش كل شيء أذبته من ذهب أو نحاس أو فضة فهو المهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other glosses of the molten drink are pus and blood, or a kind of tar.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه ضرب من القطران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may ask for water because they are thirsty; the passage compares this with being given drink from a boiling spring.
rows.anchor: أن تكون هذه الاستغاثة لأنهم إذا طلبوا ماء للشرب فيعطون هذا المهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they may seek water to cool themselves, but are given tar that covers their bodies like a garment.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يستغيثوا من حر جهنم فيطلبوا ماء يصبونه على أنفسهم للتبريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poetic line mocks the exchange by calling a painful blow a greeting.
rows.anchor: تحية بينهم ضرب وجيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drink is especially vile because a drink should relieve heat, but this one burns bodies intensely.
rows.anchor: لأن المقصود بشرب الشراب تسكين الحرارة وهذا يبلغ في احتراق الأجسام مبلغا عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of a bad resting place is that Hell is a vile gathering and abode for its companions, unbelievers and devils, unlike the good companionship and abode of Paradise.
rows.anchor: ساءت النار منزلا ومجتمعا للرفقة لأن أهل النار يجتمعون رفقاء كأهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes مرتفقا a resting place or reclining place, since a marfiq is named for what one leans on.
rows.anchor: وسمي المرفق مرفقا لأنه يتكأ عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عامر ويعقوب الحضرمي ونافع
rows.claim: Ibn Amir, Yaqub al-Hadrami, and Nafi in one transmission read لكنا هو with an alif in connected recitation; the other readers omit the alif, with no change in meaning.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر ويعقوب الحضرمي ونافع في رواية

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says the believer denies association because he sees poverty and wealth as God's dispensation, thanking Him for gifts, showing patience in trials, and refusing pride.
rows.anchor: إني لا أرى الفقر والغنى إلا منه فأحمده إذا أعطى وأصبر إذا ابتلي

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: The wealthy unbeliever's self-attribution of status and riches effectively makes a partner with God in granting honor and affluence.
rows.anchor: لما اعتز بكثرة المال والجاه فكأنه قد أثبت لله شريكا في إعطاء العز والغنى

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: The believer may be answering an idolater who denied resurrection by rejecting the worship of idols and affirming God's uniqueness.
rows.anchor: لعل ذلك الكافر مع كونه منكرا للبعث كان عابد صنم فبين هذا المؤمن فساد قوله

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: By claiming God cannot resurrect, the unbeliever makes God equal to created beings in incapacity and thereby posits a partner.
rows.anchor: لما عجز الله عن البعث والحشر فقد جعله مساويا للخلق في هذا العجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer instructs the garden owner to say ما شاء الله; ما may be conditional with an omitted result, meaning whatever God wills comes to pass.
rows.anchor: شرطية ويكون الجزاء محذوفا والتقدير أي شيء شاء الله كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ما is a relative pronoun serving as the predicate of an omitted subject: the matter is what God willed.
rows.anchor: أن تكون ما موصولة مرفوعة المحل على أنها خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Asharites infer that everything God wills occurs and what He does not will does not occur, so God did not will the unbeliever's faith, against the Mu'tazila.
rows.anchor: واحتج أصحابنا بهذا على أن كل ما أراده الله وقع وكل ما لم يرده لم يقع

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Ka'bi answers that the phrase concerns what God directly does, not human acts, comparing it with the claim that God's command cannot be nullified.
rows.anchor: ما شاء مما تولى فعله لا مما هو فعل العباد

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Ka'bi also accepts that things forbidden by God may still occur within His dominion despite not being willed.
rows.anchor: لا يمتنع أن يحصل في سلطانه ما لا يريده كما يحصل فيه ما نهى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says al-Ka'bi's reply concedes a violation of the verse's apparent meaning and wrongly equates divine willing with divine commands.
rows.anchor: ليس جوابا عن الاستدلال بل هو التزام المخالفة لظاهر النص وقياس الإرادة على الأمر

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal reads ما شاء الله as referring to the things visibly present in the garden, as in examples where a phrase points to an existing object.
rows.anchor: أي قولوا هذه حطة وإذا كان كذلك كان المراد من هذا الشيء الموجود في البستان

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: On al-Qaffal's reading, only the garden's observed objects are said to have been willed into existence; the claim is not universal.
rows.anchor: كان المراد من هذا الشيء الموجود في البستان شيء شاء الله تكوينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi judges al-Qaffal's explanation much better than the answers offered by al-Jubba'i and al-Ka'bi.
rows.anchor: وهذا التأويل الذي ذكره القفال أحسن بكثير مما ذكره الجبائي والكعبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even al-Qaffal's answer leaves the Mu'tazili difficulty: the garden may have been built through theft and grave injustice, which cannot be attributed to God's will on their doctrine.
rows.anchor: عمارة ذلك البستان ربما حصلت بالغصوب والظلم الشديد فلا يصح أيضا على قول المعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restricting God's will to the fruit's growth would narrow the text's apparent scope without evidence.
rows.anchor: إلا أن هذا تخصيص لظاهر النص من غير دليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one has power over any matter except through God's aid and empowerment.
rows.anchor: لا قوة لأحد على أمر من الأمور إلا بإعانة الله وإقداره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer tells the owner to acknowledge that the garden and its good are from God's will and grace, and God can preserve or ruin it.
rows.anchor: اعترافا بأنها وكل خير فيها بمشيئة الله وفضله فإن أمرها بيده إن شاء تركها وإن شاء خربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He should also acknowledge that his ability to build and manage the garden depends on God's support; no one has bodily or material strength apart from Him.
rows.anchor: ما قويت به على عمارتها وتدبير أمرها فهو بمعونة الله وتأييده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With أقل read in the accusative, أنا is a separator pronoun and أقل is the second object of ترى.
rows.anchor: من قرأ أقل بالنصب فقد جعل أنا فصلا وأقل مفعولا ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With أقل read in the nominative, أنا is the subject and أقل its predicate, with the clause as the second object of ترى.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بالرفع جعل قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of children shows that the earlier word نفرا includes helpers and offspring.
rows.anchor: ذكر الولد ههنا يدل على أن المراد بالنفر المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer says that if he has less wealth, children, and worldly supporters, his Lord may give him something better in this world or the next.
rows.anchor: إما في الدنيا ، وإما في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hisbanan from heaven means a divinely measured punishment and destruction; al-Zajjaj says it accounts for what the owner's hands earned.
rows.anchor: أي عذابا وتخريبا والحسبان مصدر كالغفران والبطلان

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses it as a punishment measured in recompense for what the owner's hands earned.
rows.anchor: عذاب حسبان وذلك الحسبان حسبان ما كسبت يداك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation of hisbanan is projectiles, one of which is called a hisbanah, such as lightning bolts.
rows.anchor: وقيل حسبانا أي مرامي الواحد منها حسبانة وهي الصواعق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A slippery plain is smooth ground without plants, where one's foot slips.
rows.anchor: أي فتصبح جنتك أرضا ملساء لا نبات فيها

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: The phrase about the water becoming ghawran means that it sinks and descends into the earth, and ghawr is a source-form used adjectivally.
rows.anchor: أي يغوص ويسفل في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once the water sinks, the owner cannot retrieve it or restore it to its place.
rows.anchor: أي فيصير بحيث لا تقدر على رده إلى موضعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fruit being surrounded is a metaphor for its total destruction, extended from an enemy encircling and taking control.
rows.anchor: وهو عبارة عن إهلاكه بالكلية وأصله من إحاطة العدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same idiom appears in the account of Jacob requiring his sons to be surrounded, meaning besieged by an enemy.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله : { إلا أن يحاط بكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning his palms is a metaphor for regret and grief: a deeply sorrowful person claps or rubs one hand against the other over his lost investment.
rows.anchor: وهو كناية عن الندم والحسرة فإن من عظمت حسرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The collapsed trellises may be grape arbors beneath which the walls fell, or roofs that fell onto the walls; either way the phrase means complete ruin.
rows.anchor: أي ساقطة على عروشها فيمكن أن يكون المراد بالعروش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruined man recalls the believer's declaration of God's oneness and regrets having associated a partner with his Lord.
rows.anchor: فهذا الكافر تذكر كلامه وقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruin does not prove that believers are spared affliction: most trials also befall believers, and a prophetic report says prophets, saints, then the best are most tested.
rows.anchor: خص البلاء بالأنبياء ثم الأولياء ثم الأمثل فالأمثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His regret does not establish sincere repentance: he wanted monotheism only because he thought it would preserve his garden, so God did not accept it.
rows.anchor: إنما ندم على الشرك لاعتقاده أنه لو كان موحدا غير مشرك لبقيت عليه جنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His grief is severe because he spent his life seeking worldly gain and neglecting religion; now both his worldly gain and religious opportunity are lost.
rows.anchor: لأجل أنه أنفق عمره في تحصيل الدنيا وكان معرضا في كل عمره عن طلب الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is another parable showing the world's insignificance and short duration, aimed at wealthy polytheists who boast of riches and supporters over poor believers.
rows.anchor: اضرب مثلا آخر يدل على حقارة الدنيا وقلة بقائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain makes the earth's plants grow, sway, and look beautiful, as another verse says that the earth stirs and swells after rain.
rows.anchor: وحينئذ يربو ذلك النبات ويهتز ويحسن منظره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a time the vegetation dries into hashim, broken and crumbled plant matter, then winds scatter it in every direction.
rows.anchor: هشيما ، وهو النبت المتكسر المتفتت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poem uses هشّم for crushing bread, illustrating the sense of breaking or crumbling.
rows.anchor: عمرو الذي هشم الثريد لأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's power appears in bringing the plant into being, nurturing it, and then abolishing it; worldly life likewise grows from beauty to decline and extinction.
rows.anchor: بتكوينه أولا وتنميته وسطا وإبطاله آخرا وأحوال الدنيا أيضا كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because worldly beauty inevitably declines into destruction, a rational person should not take delight in it.
rows.anchor: تظهر أولا في غاية الحسن والنضارة ثم تتزايد قليلا قليلا ثم تأخذ في الانحطاط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical explanation of باء in فاختلط به نبات الأرض is that kinds of plants mix with one another because rain strengthens and entangles them.
rows.anchor: التقدير فاختلط بعض أنواع النبات بسائر الأنواع بسبب هذا الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that water mixes with plants and plants with water until they are saturated and lush; either mingled thing may take the other's description.
rows.anchor: فاختلط ذلك الماء بالنبات واختلط ذلك النبات بالماء حتى روى ورف رفيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After refuting the unbelievers and describing their worldly and afterlife states, the surah closes by presenting the believers' condition.
rows.anchor: لما رد على أصناف الكفرة وبالغ في شرح أحوالهم في الدنيا والآخرة ختم السورة بذكر أحوال المؤمنين

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say God will create love for believers in people's hearts without their seeking ordinary causes such as kinship, friendship, or favors; this is a special honor like the awe cast into enemies' hearts.
rows.anchor: سيحدث لهم في القلوب مودة ويزرعها لهم فيها من غير تودد منهم ولا تعرض للأسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future tense may promise love after Islam because the Meccan believers were then hated by unbelievers.
rows.anchor: السين في سيجعل إما لأن السورة مكية وكان المؤمنون حينئذ ممقوتين بين الكفرة فوعدهم الله تعالى ذلك إذا جاء الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, on the Resurrection God makes believers beloved by creation as their good deeds are displayed and their records publicized.
rows.anchor: وإما أن يكون ذلك يوم القيامة يحببهم إلى خلقه بما يعرض من حسناتهم وينشر من ديوان أعمالهم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report says that when God loves a servant He tells Gabriel, who proclaims that love in heaven and earth; the same occurs when God hates someone.
rows.anchor: إذا أحب الله عبدا نادى جبريل قد أحببت فلانا فأحبوه فينادي جبريل عليه السلام بذلك في السماء والأرض

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka'b says the Torah and Gospel teach that no one is loved on earth until God begins that love and sends it down first to heaven and then earth.
rows.anchor: مكتوب في التوراة والإنجيل لا محبة لأحد في الأرض حتى يكون ابتداؤها من الله تعالى

none: surah heading and verse text only

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining the fate of those who turn away from God's remembrance, the text points to worldly examples of peoples who denied messengers as a warning.
rows.anchor: من أعرض عن ذكره كيف يحشر يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading is أفلم يهد with yāʾ; its subject is the following phrase, how many communities God destroyed.
rows.anchor: والقراءة العامة أفلم يهد بالياء المعجمة من تحت

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says the great number of destroyed peoples serves as a clear proof, admonition, and deterrent.
rows.anchor: جعل كثرة ما أهلك من القرون

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
rows.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami reads أفلم نهد with nūn, and al-Zajjaj explains it as a clear demonstration that could guide them if they reflected.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي أفلم نهد لهم بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: How many We destroyed emphasizes the great number of former generations God destroyed.
rows.anchor: فالمراد به المبالغة في كثرة من أهلكه الله تعالى من القرون الماضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh walk through the former peoples' dwellings and witness signs of their former blessings and the calamities that befell them; direct sight gives a stronger lesson.
rows.anchor: أن قريشا يشاهدون تلك الآيات العظيمة الدالة على ما كانوا عليه من النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word أولي النهى means people of intellect; Razi says it likely adds the sense of a reason that restrains its possessor from vice, while some gloss it as pious and God-fearing people.
rows.anchor: الأقرب أن للنهية مزية على العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence has fronting and postponement: without a prior divine decree and an appointed term, punishment would have become binding on them.
rows.anchor: ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك وأجل مسمى لكان لزاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior decree is God's announcement to angels and recording in the Preserved Tablet that Muhammad's people would be reprieved despite denial rather than annihilated like earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: الكلمة هي إخبار الله تعالى ملائكته وكتبه في اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One explanation for reprieve is that God knew some of Muhammad's people would believe.
rows.anchor: لأنه علم أن فيهم من يؤمن

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God knew future descendants would believe, and immediate punishment would destroy them all.
rows.anchor: علم أن في نسلهم من يؤمن ولو أنزل بهم العذاب لعمهم الهلاك

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: A further explanation is that the wisdom behind delaying punishment is hidden and known only to God.
rows.anchor: المصلحة فيه خفية لا يعلمها إلا هو

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: Sunnis say that as sovereign owner God may favor whom He wills and punish whom He wills without a causal obligation; an eternal cause would entail an eternal act, while a created cause entails regress.
rows.anchor: له بحكم المالكية أن يخص من شاء بفضله ومن شاء بعذابه من غير علة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term may mean the time of punishment in this world, namely the Battle of Badr.
rows.anchor: ولولا أجل مسمى في الدنيا لذلك العذاب وهو يوم بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the stronger view is that the appointed term is in the afterlife, since the prior decree promised delay until then.
rows.anchor: ولولا أجل مسمى في الآخرة لذلك العذب وهو أقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience is commanded in response to whatever hurts the Prophet: insults such as sorcerer, madman, or poet; denial of his prophethood; or refusal to accept his call.
rows.anchor: فيحتمل أن يكون ذلك قول بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command encourages continued patience, calling people to God, and delivering the entrusted message despite their conduct.
rows.anchor: فرغبه تعالى في الصبر وبعثه على الإدامة على الدعاء إلى الله تعالى وإبلاغ ما حمل من الرسالة

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say the patience command was abrogated by the fighting verse.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية منسوخة بآية القتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to glorify with praise is comparable to the instruction to seek aid through patience and prayer.
rows.anchor: وهو نظير قوله : { واستعينوا بالصبر والصلواة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase with your Lord's praise is circumstantial: the Prophet glorifies while praising God for enabling and assisting him.
rows.anchor: في موضع الحال وأنت حامد لربك على أن وفقك للتسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorification follows the command to be patient because remembrance of God gives solace and rest; believers find no rest apart from meeting God.
rows.anchor: إنما أمر عقيب الصبر بالتسبيح لأن ذكر الله تعالى يفيد السلوة والراحة

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most commentators take glorification here to mean prayer and offer three accounts of how the prayer times are specified.
rows.anchor: فالأكثرون على أن المراد منه الصلاة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse establishes exactly five prayers: dawn before sunrise, noon and afternoon before sunset, and sunset and night prayers during the night; the day-end phrase reinforces dawn and sunset.
rows.anchor: دخلت الصلوات الخمس فيه ، فقبل طلوع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second prayer reading includes the five obligatory prayers in the two daylight periods and treats the night watches and day ends as additional voluntary prayers.
rows.anchor: أن الآية تدل على الصلوات الخمس وزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third prayer reading identifies dawn, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers, leaving the noon prayer outside the verse.
rows.anchor: أنها تدل على أقل من الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi judges the first interpretation, which includes exactly the five prayers, the strongest and best supported.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول أقوى وبالاعتبار أولى

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says glorification may instead mean declaring God's transcendence and majesty at these times, not ritual prayer.
rows.anchor: لا يبعد حمله على التنزيه والإجلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says Abu Muslim's reading is closer to the apparent sense and context: after abuse and denial, the Prophet should proclaim God's transcendence and call people to Him at all times.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول أقرب إلى الظاهر وإلى ما تقدم ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is the best time for remembrance because people are quiet, movement and sensory activity cease, and worship then is harder for body and soul and so earns greater reward.
rows.anchor: أفضل الذكر ما كان بالليل لأن الجمعية فيه أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer to why the verse says ends of the day in plural is that the minimum plural can mean two.
rows.anchor: من الناس من قال أقل الجمع اثنان فسقط السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer is that the two ends recur every day, so they are expressed in the plural.
rows.anchor: إنما جمع لأنه يتكرر في كل نهار ويعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One gloss of so that you may be pleased is a promise of elevated favor, like a sovereign telling a servant that service may bring him benefit.
rows.anchor: يا فلان اشتغل بالخدمة فلعلك تنتفع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second gloss is that the Prophet may be pleased with the reward he receives.
rows.anchor: لعلك ترضى ما تنال من الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third gloss is that he may be pleased with the intercession granted to him.
rows.anchor: لعلك ترضى ما تنال من الشفاعة

rows.speaker: الكسائي وعاصم
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i and Asim read ترضى with a damma on the tāʾ; the meaning is unchanged, since God making the Prophet content is equivalent to being pleased with him.
rows.anchor: لعلك ترضى بضم التاء والمعنى لا يختلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although blessings too are trials, Arabic often calls a hardship a fitna because the term usually applies to what feels burdensome; the hypocrite recognizes only worldly good and harm.
rows.anchor: إنما يطلق اسم البلاء على ما يثقل على الطبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection asks how someone can turn back if he never truly accepted Islam in the first place.
rows.anchor: إذا كانت الآية في المنافق فما معنى قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning back means changing what one says: he praised the religion before hardship, then disparages it when trouble comes, which is a real reversal.
rows.anchor: المراد أنه أظهر بلسانه خلاف ما كان أظهره فصار يذم الدين عند الشدة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil asks why the verse contrasts good with fitna rather than saying that evil befalls the person.
rows.anchor: الخير هو ضد الشر فلما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not call the hardship evil because hardship is not inherently morally ugly; the verse uses a description that does not imply ugliness.
rows.anchor: لما كانت الشدة ليست بقبيحة لم يقل تعالى وإن أصابه شر بل وصفه بما لا يفيد فيه القبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He loses worldly honor, dignity, spoils, and eligibility for testimony, leadership, and judgment, and loses protection for his property and blood; in the next life he loses lasting reward and gains lasting punishment.
rows.anchor: يخسر في الدنيا العزة والكرامة وإصابة الغنيمة وأهلية الشهادة والإمامة والقضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who calls on something besides God that neither harms nor benefits is most likely a polytheist worshipping idols, which makes the passage unlikely to concern a Jew.
rows.anchor: الأقرب أنه المشرك الذي يعبد الأوثان وهذا كالدلالة على أن الآية لم ترد في اليهودي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the passage likely concerns polytheists who attached themselves to the Messenger hypocritically.
rows.anchor: في المشركين الذين انقطعوا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manifest remote error may describe the magnitude of their misguidance, or their distance from correctness, since errors differ in how far they lie from truth.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يعني بذلك بعد ضلالهم عن الصواب لأن جميعه وإن كان يشترك في أنه خطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase remote error is metaphorical, comparing their misguidance to a traveler lost for a long distance in the wilderness.
rows.anchor: واستعير الضلال البعيد من ضلال من أبعد في التيه ضالا وطالت وبعدت مسافة ضلاله
